stem: Which breeding record best supports later evaluation of whether a selected trait is repeatable?
choices: Parentage, generation, environment, measured phenotype, selection criteria, and progeny results
Parentage, harvest date, breeder notes, a representative photograph, and the final decision to keep or discard the selected plant
Generation, cultivar label, flowering duration, plant height, and the environmental set points used during the selection cycle
Parent identity, seed count, container size, nutrient program, and a summary rating of the selected trait without progeny follow-up
rationale: A useful selection record links pedigree and generation to the environment, measured traits, explicit criteria, and later progeny evidence so decisions can be evaluated rather than reconstructed from memory.
